query: Why do expense decline rates differ across departments?

judge.outcome_variable: dept_decline_rate (expense decline rate, varying across departments)

per_column.name: is_declined
per_column.rationale: Row-level indicator of the decline outcome; it is the raw outcome event, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause surfaced from the data (whether an expense has a source_id) that could plausibly drive decline likelihood; not named in the query, so it functions as a possible treatment/explanatory factor.

per_column.name: dept_total_count
per_column.rationale: Department volume can plausibly relate to both processing behavior/treatment prevalence and decline rate; but here it is essentially the denominator used to compute the outcome rate, making it more mechanical than a genuine common cause.

per_column.name: dept_declined_count
per_column.rationale: This is the numerator of the decline rate — a direct component of the outcome, not an independent cause or confounder.

per_column.name: dept_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: This is the focus outcome itself (departmental decline rate), directly named/implied by the query.

per_column.name: processing_days
per_column.rationale: Processing time is plausibly on the causal path (a department's practices affect processing time, which affects decline decisions); treating it as a confounder would be a mistake — it is more naturally a mediator.

judge.rationale: The added columns are overwhelmingly mechanical decompositions of the outcome itself: is_declined, dept_declined_count, dept_decline_rate are the numerator/denominator/rate that define the very quantity the query asks about, and do not set up a causal estimation. A plausible treatment (has_source_id) is surfaced from the data, satisfying part (a) weakly. However, the causal claim requires genuine CONFOUNDERS — common causes of both a treatment and the outcome — surfaced from the data. None qualify: dept_total_count is essentially the rate denominator rather than a true common cause, and processing_days is best read as a mediator on the causal path, not a confounder. There are no variables (e.g., expense category mix, amount, user, requestor seniority) surfaced as adjustment variables that jointly cause a treatment and the decline outcome. Thus the decisive test — surfacing non-query confounders that must be adjusted — is essentially not met.
